messages.content: Determine the winner in a Poker game with John having a Hand of 8♥, 10♥, J♥, Q♥, K♥ and Mike having 9♠, J♠, 10♠, Q♠, K♠.

function.name: card_games_poker_determine_winner
function.description: Determines the winner in a game of Poker based on the cards in each players' hands. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

hand1.description: The list of cards (as strings) in first player's hand. E.g ['10♠', 'J♠']

hand2.description: The list of cards (as strings) in second player's hand. E.g ['9♥', '10♥']

message.content:
Mike wins.  
John’s hand is a flush (8♥‑10♥‑J♥‑Q♥‑K♥).  
Mike’s hand is a straight‑flush (9♠‑10♠‑J♠‑Q♠‑K♠), which outranks a plain flush.
message.reasoning:
We need to determine winner. John has 8♥,10♥,J♥,Q♥,K♥. That's a straight flush from 8 to K? Actually 8-10-J-Q-K is a straight flush (8-9-10-J-Q-K? Wait missing 9). Straight flush requires consecutive ranks. John's cards: 8,10,J,Q,K. Missing 9. So not a straight flush. It's a flush (all hearts) but not straight. Highest card K. Mike has 9♠, J♠,10♠,Q♠,K♠. That's also a flush (spades). Highest card K. But Mike has 9,10,J,Q,K. That's also a straight? 9-10-J-Q-K is a straight. And it's a straight flush because all same suit. So Mike has a straight flush (9-10-J-Q-K). John has a flush. Straight flush beats flush. So Mike wins.

Thus answer: Mike wins.
